occupants.value: An inferred household; no name is claimed
occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the dwelling of an inferred mason's household (3 of 4 this layer infers): hh_inf_mason_north_03 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

residents.name: The Ingalls household — a reconstructed mason (north division)
residents.why: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_north_d4_012 is an anonymous reconstructed roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.
residents.basis: An anonymous roof of the reconstruction programme, ADOPTED by this household rather than raised for it. The roof's own existence and position stay conjectural; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit.

persons.name: Amos Ingalls
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. THE NAME IS INVENTED TOO, and `name_basis` beside it says so and says which pool it came from: this record used to carry a bare designation instead, on the reasoning that a surname would make it look like the documented layer, but a town of designations does not read as a town and the grade, this note and name_basis all say plainly which layer this is. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE THIRD OF 4 MASON HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER RECONSTRUCTS. EVERY FRAME HOUSE IN THE TOWN CARRIES A HEARTH AND A STACK. Blodgett's yard on the north side has made brick since the spring of 1833 (Andreas, scan p. 1161), and the most ambitious building under way on the scene date - the Lake House - is going up in brick in a town otherwise built of logs and boards. The documented layer holds one mason. Three more mason households are inferred: the chimney trade alone, at 398 dwellings, is more work than one man's.

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - third of 4 mason households in this layer, in the north division. EVERY FRAME HOUSE IN THE TOWN CARRIES A HEARTH AND A STACK. Blodgett's yard on the north side has made brick since the spring of 1833 (Andreas, scan p. 1161), and the most ambitious building under way on the scene date - the Lake House - is going up in brick in a town otherwise built of logs and boards. The documented layer holds one mason. Three more mason households are inferred: the chimney trade alone, at 398 dwellings, is more work than one man's. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
